title: What If Earth Flew Through a Comet's Poison Tail? 1910 Did

scenes.text: What if Earth passed through a comet's poisonous tail? In 1910, people thought it would.
Cyanogen, a toxic gas, was confirmed in Halley's tail in February 1910. Newspapers warned it could poison the planet.
People bought comet pills made of sugar and quinine. Bartenders even claimed whiskey would protect you.
Scientists knew better. Comet tails hold very little gas, and the cyanogen would break down in the upper atmosphere.
On the night of May 18 to 19, the tail swept past Earth. Air Liquide tested Paris air and found no toxic gas.
Later calculations showed the tail missed Earth by at least 400,000 kilometers. The panic was the only thing that spread.

description:
What if Earth flew through a comet's poisonous tail?
In 1910, newspapers warned Halley's Comet could poison the air. Comet pills sold out, and on the night it passed, tests found no toxic gas.
What should we run through next?
